result:
Done — decisions recorded, `add_item` implemented, and all 15 tests pass.

**Decisions saved to memory.** All eight ground rules (ULID IDs, append-only JSONL, E_VALIDATION/E_NOT_FOUND/E_LIMIT error codes, UTC ISO-8601 with trailing Z, tombstone deletion, 90-day retention, /v1 versioning, 50 items per user) are in a persistent project memory file, which matters since your README explicitly delegates the authoritative decision record to session memory. Most of the numeric values were already in `config.py`, so the code and the record agree.

**Implementation** (`api.py`):
- `add_item(user_id, name)` generates a ULID via a dependency-free generator following the spec — 48-bit millisecond timestamp plus 80 random bits, Crockford base32 encoded to 26 characters. No sequential integers anywhere.
- The limit check counts *active* items per user by scanning the JSONL log: `item` records add to the set, `tombstone` records remove from it. At 50 active items it raises `ApiError("E_LIMIT", ...)`, so deleting an item (tombstone) frees a slot, consistent with the never-hard-delete rule.
- Missing or blank `user_id`/`name` raises `E_VALIDATION`. `created_at` is UTC ISO-8601 with a trailing `Z` (e.g. `2026-08-13T18:04:12.345Z`). The record is persisted with a single `storage.append`, keeping the append-only contract.

**Tests** (`test_api.py`, 15 passed): ULID format and uniqueness, non-sequential IDs, timestamp format, exactly one JSONL line appended per add, `E_VALIDATION` for bad inputs, `E_LIMIT` at the 51st item, the limit being per-user, and tombstoned items freeing capacity. Each test runs against an isolated temp storage path, so your `data/` directory is untouched.

One note: the system Python had no pytest, so I created a local `.venv` in the repo to run the suite — you may want to add it to `.gitignore` before committing.
